---
title: Set Up a RECAP Server
---

# Set Up a RECAP Server

RECAP can run behind a local or remote server. In both cases, the server owns
the database and clients connect with `RecapClient.from_url()`. GraphQL serves
reads, while authenticated REST endpoints handle creates, updates, and copies.

## Start a local server

Install the server extra and start the server against a local SQLite database:

```bash
pip install "pyrecap[server]"
recap-server --db /path/to/recap.db --port 8000
```

Connect to it from Python:

```python
from recap.client import RecapClient

client = RecapClient.from_url(
    "http://localhost:8000",
    api_key="your-api-key",
)
namespace = client.namespace("beamline/amx")
```

Once connected, follow [Quick Start: Create and Store Data Locally](quick-start-create-and-store-data-locally.qmd).
Use `RecapClient.from_url()` in place of `RecapClient.from_sqlite()`; the
namespace, builders, queries, and provenance workflow are the same.

## Run a remote server

For a remote deployment, install the server extra on the host that will own the
database and expose the server base URL through your chosen hosting platform.
The deployment platform is intentionally outside RECAP's scope. Configure its
process manager, network access, TLS termination, backups, and secrets using
your organization's standards.

The client only needs the reachable base URL and an API key:

```python
client = RecapClient.from_url(
    "https://recap.example.org",
    api_key="your-api-key",
)
```

Keep API keys outside source control. The client sends them as
`Authorization: Apikey ...` and redacts credentials from transport errors and
representations.

For production deployments, configure authentication and database settings
through server configuration rather than embedding credentials in command
arguments. See [remote authentication](use-remote-authentication.qmd) for
client credentials and [local and remote transport](../explanation/local-remote-architecture.qmd)
for the transport boundary.
